quests.instruction: Tom says there's no wind today because he can't see any.
quests.question: Why isn't that a good way to check?
options: Wind appears when the Sun goes down
Wind is made out of tiny falling raindrops
Wind is invisible; you notice what it moves
Wind blows on mountains but not on plains
quests.correctAnswer: Wind is invisible; you notice what it moves
quests.hint: Picture how you know the wind is there on a flag day.
quests.explanation: Wind is just moving air, which has no colour. We find it by seeing, hearing or feeling its effects.
quests.funFact: Wind blows because air moves from areas of higher pressure to areas of lower pressure.

quests.instruction: Leaves rustle softly and a few thin twigs sway, but the large branches stay still.
quests.question: How would you describe this wind?
options: A gentle breeze
A strong gale
A violent storm
Perfectly calm air
quests.correctAnswer: A gentle breeze
quests.hint: Only the lightest parts of the tree are moving.
quests.explanation: A gentle breeze moves leaves and twigs but is too weak to bend big branches.
quests.funFact: In 1805, Admiral Francis Beaufort invented a scale that describes wind by what it does to things.

quests.instruction: The Sun warms some ground much more than other ground nearby.
quests.question: What can this uneven warming cause in the air?
options: Air starts to move and makes wind
Clouds stop moving across the sky
Rain freezes into snow in the sky
Air slowly disappears from the ground
quests.correctAnswer: Air starts to move and makes wind
quests.hint: Warm air and cooler air don't behave in the same way.
quests.explanation: Warm air rises and cooler air flows in to take its place. That moving air is wind.
quests.funFact: A sea breeze happens because land heats up faster than the sea.

quests.instruction: A row of white turbines turns slowly on a hill. Kiran wonders what turns them.
quests.question: What pushes the blades around?
options: Water inside them
Heat from the Sun
Gravity from below
Moving air
quests.correctAnswer: Moving air
quests.hint: Think of what turns a pinwheel when you blow on it.
quests.explanation: Moving air pushes against the blades and makes the turbine spin.
quests.funFact: Wind turbines turn the movement of air into electricity.

quests.instruction: A dandelion puff breaks apart as a breeze passes through the field.
quests.question: How is the wind helping the plant?
options: It carries the seeds to new places
It waters the roots of the plant
It warms the soil around the seeds
It pulls the roots deeper into the soil
quests.correctAnswer: It carries the seeds to new places
quests.hint: Imagine where the little parachutes are going.
quests.explanation: Many plants rely on wind to scatter their seeds, so new plants can grow far from the parent.
quests.funFact: Maple seeds spin like helicopters, which helps them travel farther on the wind.

quests.instruction: A small boat moves across the bay with no engine and no oars.
quests.question: What is pushing the boat along?
options: Fish pulling it
Wind against the sail
Heat from the Sun
Waves made by rain
quests.correctAnswer: Wind against the sail
quests.hint: Focus on what fills a big piece of cloth in the air.
quests.explanation: A sail catches moving air, and the push of the wind drives the boat forward.
quests.funFact: Wind-powered ships crossed oceans for thousands of years before engines were invented.

quests.instruction: The flag on the school roof points toward the east.
quests.question: Which way is the wind blowing from?
options: From the north
From the south
From the west
From the east
quests.correctAnswer: From the west
quests.hint: The wind pushes the flag away from where it starts.
quests.explanation: Wind pushes a flag in the direction it is blowing to. So the wind comes from the opposite side, the west.
quests.funFact: A wind from the west is called a westerly.

quests.instruction: Mia has no tools and wants to find out which way the wind is blowing.
quests.question: Which trick would work?
options: Count the clouds overhead
Listen for birdsong
Measure the length of her shadow
Toss a pinch of grass into the air
quests.correctAnswer: Toss a pinch of grass into the air
quests.hint: Remember something light enough to be carried.
quests.explanation: Light grass or leaves drift along with the wind, so you can see which way the air is moving.
quests.funFact: Sailors have long used flags and streamers to show which way the wind blows.

quests.instruction: Sam stands in the park with his back to the wind.
quests.question: Where is the wind coming from?
options: Both sides equally
In front of him
Behind him
Straight above him
quests.correctAnswer: Behind him
quests.hint: Which way will the air push him when he's facing away?
quests.explanation: If the wind is at your back, it comes from behind you and pushes you gently forward.
quests.funFact: A wind in your face is called a headwind, and it makes cycling harder.

quests.instruction: The class plans a kite-flying afternoon on the hill.
quests.question: Which wind is best for flying a kite?
options: Wild gusts and heavy rain
A steady, moderate breeze
No wind at all
A calm, still morning
quests.correctAnswer: A steady, moderate breeze
quests.hint: A kite needs air moving across it, but not so much that it's hard to control.
quests.explanation: A steady moderate breeze lifts a kite and keeps it up. Too little wind won't lift it and too much makes it hard to control.
quests.funFact: The oldest kites were flown in China more than 2,000 years ago.

quests.instruction: Two friends want to fly kites. One suggests a field next to power lines and another picks an open, empty field.
quests.question: Where is the safest place to fly a kite?
options: A field right beside power lines
An open field away from power lines
A road with passing cars
The flat top of a building
quests.correctAnswer: An open field away from power lines
quests.hint: Kite strings can reach where they shouldn't.
quests.explanation: Kite strings can touch power lines, which is dangerous. Open space far from lines, roads and roofs is safest.
quests.funFact: A kite string can carry electricity if it touches power lines, so kite flyers keep far away from them.

quests.instruction: While flying a kite, Lila feels the string pulling harder and harder in her hands.
quests.question: What has probably changed?
options: The clouds have cleared
The Sun has become hotter
The wind has become stronger
The air has become still
quests.correctAnswer: The wind has become stronger
quests.hint: What pushes on the kite and pulls on the string?
quests.explanation: A stronger wind pushes harder on the kite, so it pulls harder on the string.
quests.funFact: The lifting force that holds up a kite also helps airplane wings stay in the air.

quests.instruction: Dev notices that the sea has bigger waves on a windy day than on a calm one.
quests.question: Why are the waves bigger on a windy day?
options: The sea becomes saltier on windy days
The sea water gets much warmer
Rain fills up the sea from above
Wind pushes on the water's surface
quests.correctAnswer: Wind pushes on the water's surface
quests.hint: Notice what happens to a bowl of water when you blow across it.
quests.explanation: Wind drags across the water's surface and builds ripples into waves. Stronger winds make bigger waves.
quests.funFact: Most ocean waves are made by wind blowing across the water.

quests.instruction: A wind farm has been built on a high hill and another at sea.
quests.question: Why are wind turbines often placed on hills or at sea?
options: The sea water powers the blades directly
Hills are warmer than the flat land
The clouds sit closer to the ground there
Winds are often stronger and steadier there
quests.correctAnswer: Winds are often stronger and steadier there
quests.hint: Turbines work best where there is plenty of moving air.
quests.explanation: Few buildings or trees block the wind on hills and at sea, so air moves faster and more steadily.
quests.funFact: The biggest modern turbine blades are longer than a football pitch.

quests.instruction: A cold wind squeezes through a small gap under the door and makes a whistling sound.
quests.question: Why does the wind whistle there?
options: The wind is trapped inside the wall
Cold air carries sound more loudly
Air is squeezed through a narrow space
Rain is trapped inside the door frame
quests.correctAnswer: Air is squeezed through a narrow space
quests.hint: Consider what happens when you blow through a small gap between your lips.
quests.explanation: When air is forced through a narrow gap, it vibrates and makes a whistling sound.
quests.funFact: A wind harp, called an aeolian harp, makes music when wind passes over its strings.

quests.instruction: A strong wind is blowing as the class walks back from the park.
quests.question: Which spot is the safest to stand in?
options: Beside a wobbly fence at the road's edge
Clear of tall trees and loose signs
Under a heavy branch hanging overhead
Right beneath the branches of a tall tree
quests.correctAnswer: Clear of tall trees and loose signs
quests.hint: Picture what might fall or be blown over.
quests.explanation: Strong winds can snap branches or knock things over, so stay clear of trees and loose objects.
quests.funFact: Gusts can break weak branches without any warning.

quests.instruction: The forecast says strong gusts will arrive this evening, and the family has chairs and a light table in the garden.
quests.question: What should they do with the garden furniture?
options: Stack the chairs higher on the table
Leave everything where it is for now
Bring light items inside or tie them down
Open all the umbrellas to hold them down
quests.correctAnswer: Bring light items inside or tie them down
quests.hint: Imagine which items could fly away.
quests.explanation: Strong wind can lift light objects and throw them around, so moving them indoors keeps them and people safe.
quests.funFact: Strong wind can slide even heavy garden furniture across the ground.

quests.instruction: Dust swirls up from a dry field on a gusty day and Nora feels it stinging her eyes.
quests.question: What's a good way to protect her eyes?
options: Wear glasses and turn away from the wind
Stare into the wind and keep blinking
Rub her eyes hard with both hands
Run faster straight into the dust
quests.correctAnswer: Wear glasses and turn away from the wind
quests.hint: Focus on keeping dust from getting in.
quests.explanation: Glasses block dust, and turning away keeps the wind from blowing grit into your eyes.
quests.funFact: Dust from the Sahara can be carried by wind across the Atlantic Ocean.

quests.instruction: A gardener describes four types of wind to a class.
quests.question: Which one is the strongest?
options: Calm air with straight smoke
A soft puff stirring leaves
A light breeze lifting hair
A gale that makes walking hard
quests.correctAnswer: A gale that makes walking hard
quests.hint: Remember how much effort each wind takes to walk against.
quests.explanation: A gale is a very strong wind that can make walking difficult. The others are gentle or calm.
quests.funFact: Wind speeds are usually reported in kilometres per hour or knots.

quests.instruction: A weather chart shows wind speeds for four days: Monday 3 km/h, Tuesday 18 km/h, Wednesday 45 km/h, Thursday 70 km/h.
quests.question: Which day is best for flying a kite?
options: Tuesday
Thursday
Wednesday
Monday
quests.correctAnswer: Tuesday
quests.hint: Too little wind can't lift a kite and too much is hard to control.
quests.explanation: Eighteen kilometres per hour is a good steady breeze. Three is too weak, and forty-five or seventy are too strong.
quests.funFact: Kite flyers often like winds of about 10 to 30 kilometres per hour.

quests.instruction: A paper plate, a brick, a full bucket and a stone bench are in a garden during a strong wind.
quests.question: Which one is most likely to blow away?
options: The solid stone bench
The empty paper plate
The heavy clay brick
The full bucket of water
quests.correctAnswer: The empty paper plate
quests.hint: Which one is light enough for air to push?
quests.explanation: Light objects are pushed around much more easily by moving air than heavy ones.
quests.funFact: A weightier object needs a much stronger wind to move it.

quests.instruction: A farmer plants rows of tall trees along the edge of her fields.
quests.question: What do these trees do for the crops?
options: They warm the soil during the night
They make clouds form above the field
They slow the wind and protect the plants
They make it rain more often there
quests.correctAnswer: They slow the wind and protect the plants
quests.hint: Notice what the trees do to moving air.
quests.explanation: A line of trees acts like a shield, slowing the wind so it doesn't damage crops or blow soil away.
quests.funFact: Rows of trees used this way are called windbreaks.

quests.instruction: An eagle circles high in the sky without flapping its wings once.
quests.question: How does it stay up so easily?
options: It is lighter than most clouds
It rides rising currents of warm air
It uses tiny jets in its feathers
It pushes the clouds beneath it
quests.correctAnswer: It rides rising currents of warm air
quests.hint: Consider what warm air does when it rises.
quests.explanation: Large birds can glide on columns of rising warm air called thermals, so they save energy.
quests.funFact: Some birds use thermals to climb thousands of metres without flapping.

quests.instruction: A wind is blowing toward a town from a range of snowy mountains.
quests.question: What is the air likely to feel like in town?
options: Cooler
Heavier
Quieter
Hotter
quests.correctAnswer: Cooler
quests.hint: Wind often carries the feel of the place it started from.
quests.explanation: Wind brings air from where it began. Air from cold, snowy mountains tends to bring cooler weather.
quests.funFact: A wind often carries weather from the area where it began.

quests.instruction: On a hot afternoon at the beach, Mia notices a cool breeze coming in from the sea.
quests.question: Why does the breeze blow from the sea?
options: Ships and boats stir up the air over the water
The Sun drops into the water and cools it
Land warms faster, so cooler sea air moves in
Rain is drifting in from far out at sea
quests.correctAnswer: Land warms faster, so cooler sea air moves in
quests.hint: Picture which heats up faster, sand or water.
quests.explanation: Sand heats up faster than water. Warm air over the land rises, and cooler air from the sea flows in.
quests.funFact: At night, the breeze often reverses and blows from the land to the sea.

quests.instruction: At a small airport, a windsock sticks out straight and stiff from its pole.
quests.question: What does that tell you about the wind?
options: It is blowing strongly
There is almost no wind
The air is cold
Rain is about to start
quests.correctAnswer: It is blowing strongly
quests.hint: Imagine how the sock looks when the wind is calm.
quests.explanation: A windsock fills and stands out when wind is strong, and it hangs limp when the air is calm.
quests.funFact: Windsocks help pilots see which way the wind is blowing and how strong it is.

quests.instruction: Long ago, farmers tossed harvested grain into the air on breezy days.
quests.question: Why did they do that?
options: The wind cooled the grain down
The wind counted all the seeds
The wind helped the grain grow
Wind blew off the light husks
quests.correctAnswer: Wind blew off the light husks
quests.hint: Wind moves light things farther than heavy ones.
quests.explanation: The light husks blew away and the heavier grain fell back down. This is called winnowing.
quests.funFact: Winnowing is still used in some places today.

quests.instruction: The forecast warns of strong gusts this afternoon, and the class had planned several activities.
quests.question: Which plan would be most affected?
options: An outdoor lunch with paper plates
Painting pictures inside the classroom
Reading a story on the carpet inside
A quiet board game in the classroom
quests.correctAnswer: An outdoor lunch with paper plates
quests.hint: Which activity involves light things outside?
quests.explanation: Gusts would blow paper plates and napkins away. Indoor activities aren't affected.
quests.funFact: Gusts are short bursts of faster wind that come and go.

quests.instruction: Kiran's kite is high in the sky when the wind suddenly drops to almost nothing.
quests.question: What will most likely happen to the kite?
options: It will turn into a small cloud
It will climb even higher up
It will fly faster across the sky
It will sink toward the ground
quests.correctAnswer: It will sink toward the ground
quests.hint: A kite needs moving air to stay up.
quests.explanation: Without moving air, a kite can't stay lifted, so it drifts down.
quests.funFact: A kite needs air moving over it to stay up.

quests.instruction: It is a cold, windy day and the school is planning an outdoor walk.
quests.question: Which is a good outer layer?
options: A wide straw hat
A windproof jacket
A thin cotton scarf
A mesh sports shirt
quests.correctAnswer: A windproof jacket
quests.hint: Focus on what blocks wind from reaching you.
quests.explanation: A windproof jacket stops the wind from carrying away your body heat.
quests.funFact: Windproof fabrics keep a layer of warm air close to your body.
